title: alerter-channels-thresholds-matrix-draft
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working sketch for the alerts/notifications/SLO mapping UX that sits in Console -> Observability -> Alerts. Goal: reduce config complexity for engineers who need predictable notification behavior across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Focus areas: channel mapping (who gets what, when), SLO->threshold recommendations, policy templates, and a compact visual matrix that makes dependencies obvious.

Background/context:
- Current Console has basic notification hooks (Slack, PagerDuty, email) but lacks an opinionated SLO-to-notification path and escalation policy composer.
- Pain observed in support tickets: teams misconfigure channels, duplicate alerts across channels, and set thresholds that generate noisy paging during maintenance windows.
- Product objective: Enable safe defaults + quick customizations so teams can get reasonable alerting without expert SRE help.

Design principles (quick):
- Defaults first: provide SLO-based defaults (recommended thresholds and severity) that are editable.
- Least surprise: channels visible in a single compact matrix view with per-channel overrides.
- Auditable: every policy shows last edited, owner, and linked runbook.
- Safe-by-default escalation: gentle initial notifications (email/Slack) then escalate to on-call (PagerDuty) only when sustained or severe.
- Multi-deploy support: policies can be global or constrained to Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Key concepts and terminology (as we will use them):
- Policy: top-level object that ties an alert rule to SLOs, channels, thresholds, and escalation rules.
- Channel: delivery endpoint (Slack webhook, PagerDuty service, email list, webhook).
- Threshold: numeric/relative value that triggers the policy (e.g., error rate > 2% for 5m).
- Severity: info/warning/critical mapping used for routing and UI emphasis.
- Escalation step: sequence step for escalation (notify, then wait 5m, then escalate).

Wireframe notes (sketch -> components):
1) Policy list (left pane): compact cards showing policy name, linked SLO(s), active channels (icons), severity ribbon, and quick actions (duplicate, mute, edit).
2) Middle pane: matrix view. Columns = channels; rows = SLOs / alert rules. Cell content = configured threshold + severity badge. Click cell to open a contextual mini-editor with inline controls: threshold input, severity dropdown, mute toggle, channel-level delay (e.g., notify after X seconds). Hover shows last triggered timestamp and a sample recent alert.
3) Right pane: policy editor (open when create/edit). Sections: metadata (name, owner, scope), SLO bindings (pick one or many), rule selector (or custom metric expression), channel assignments (drag from channel list into matrix), escalation timeline (graphical stepper), runtime options (snooze windows, dedupe window, auto-resolve window), audit/runbook links.
4) Quick template drawer (bottom): one-click templates ("SLO breach - page on critical", "High latency - notify slack only", "Cost surge - email and slack") with brief descriptions and estimated cost impact guidance.

Suggested defaults (SLO-driven):
- For availability SLOs (>= 99.9%): warning at 0.5x error budget burn per 1h, critical at full error budget within 1h. Channels: warning -> Slack, critical -> PagerDuty + Slack.
- For latency SLOs: warning at P95 > target * 1.2 for 10m, critical at P95 > target * 1.5 for 5m. Channels: warning -> Slack, critical -> PagerDuty.
- For freshness/throughput SLOs: recommend longer dedupe window; only escalate if condition persists across two windows.
Rationale: reduce immediate paging for transient blips while ensuring persistent degradations page on-call.

Channel mapping matrix (interaction rules):
- Default channel mode: inherit from policy template.
- Channel override: cell-level override wins. UI to highlight overridden cells in bold + orange dot.
- Global mute: policy-level mute hides notifications but retains recording for audit.
- Maintenance windows: allow team-level calendar/CRON entry that suppresses notify to PagerDuty but still logs occurrences.

Escalation builder (mini-UX spec):
- Step builder uses a draggable timeline: add step -> choose channel(s) -> set wait/delay -> add condition (e.g., only escalate if count >= N or if severity escalated).
- Immediate notify step allowed for "critical" severity only.
- Guardrails: prevent final step from being purely email for critical policies (warn modal).

Telemetry / Event model to capture (for product/eng):
- policy.view, policy.create, policy.edit, policy.apply-template, channel.add, channel.test-send, cell.override, escalation.step-add, policy.mute, policy.delete, policy.deploy.
- For each policy.trigger event capture: policy_id, SLO_id, threshold_value, severity, channels_notified, escalation_path_taken, duration.

Accessibility & performance considerations:
- Matrix should be keyboard navigable with aria labels on cells.
- Provide condensed mode for teams with many SLOs; allow filters (by service, by owner, by severity).
- Virtualize rows to keep matrix responsive for 1000+ rules.

Backlog grooming notes (candidate tickets and priorities):
1) RINF-942: Policy matrix UI + mini-editor (M): 5 pts. MVP: read/write simple thresholds, show icons, cell hover. (linked above)
2) RINF-947: Escalation timeline builder component (H): 8 pts. Needs drag-and-drop, step validation, persistence.
3) RINF-951: SLO->threshold recommendation engine (M): 5 pts. Start with heuristics; later connect to Optimize.
4) RINF-960: Channel test harness and webhook verifier (L): 3 pts. Send test payloads, show response.
5) RINF-971: Templates & team-shared library (M): 3 pts. UX for save/share.
6) RINF-983: Maintenance window calendar integration (L): 5 pts. Sync w/ Google Calendar & Team schedules.
7) RINF-990: Audit log UI for policies (L): 3 pts. Show diffs, who changed what.
Priority key: H = high (customer-visible risk), M = medium, L = low.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Do we want to support per-environment policies (prod vs staging) with inheritance? UX implication: show collapsed inheritance lanes in matrix or separate tabs?
- How aggressive should SLO->threshold defaults be? Risk: too strict -> pages; too lenient -> missed SLO breaches.
- Should the escalation builder allow conditional routing based on calendar/on-call metadata (e.g., route to alternate team if primary is out)?
- Integration with Redwood Optimize: can we surface cost/regression risk when enabling high-frequency alerts?

Acceptance criteria (for MVP matrix + editor):
- Users can create a policy and bind it to one SLO.
- Users can assign at least three channel types and set per-channel delay.
- Matrix displays policy-cell threshold and severity; hover gives last-trigger preview.
- Telemetry emitted for create/edit/trigger with required fields.
- Policy changes are auditable and show owner + last modified.

Next steps / immediate actionables:
- Design: produce a mid-fidelity mock of the matrix and mini-editor (Priya) - due 2025-02-21.
- Eng: spike for virtualized matrix rendering and telemetry schema (Evan) - due 2025-02-28.
- PM: finalize SLO heuristics doc for defaults and publish to Confluence (Maya) - due 2025-02-18.
- Schedule a 60-minute cross-functional review to validate escalation UX and template language (invite: eng, design, SRE) - target week of 2025-02-24.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally opinionated; push back if the defaults feel too prescriptive. We want to prevent common misconfigs.
- Keep examples concrete when providing feedback (e.g., suggest a concrete threshold change instead of "less aggressive").

Appendix: example policy (text):
Name: "prod-api - availability breach -> page"
Owner: "Platform SRE"
Scope: Production only
SLOs: prod-api availability (99.95%)
Rule: error_rate > 0.2% over 5m
Channels: Slack (#prod-api-alerts) [immediate], PagerDuty (prod-api) [delay 3m], Email (sre-ops) [daily digest]
Escalation: Slack immediate -> if breach persists 3m -> page PagerDuty -> if persists 15m -> page manager escalation list
Runtime: Deduplicate window 300s, auto-resolve after 10m of normal metric

End of draft.
